title: WannaCry Ransomware
description: A worldwide cyberattack by the WannaCry ransomware cryptoworm, which targeted computers running the Microsoft Windows operating system by encrypting data and demanding ransom payments in the Bitcoin cryptocurrency.

title: Emotet
description: Originally a banking trojan, Emotet evolved into a modular botnet and malware distributor. It often spreads via spam emails containing malicious attachments or links.
prevention: Train employees to recognize phishing emails.

title: Stuxnet
description: A malicious computer worm that targeted SCADA systems and was responsible for causing substantial damage to Iran's nuclear program.

title: Spear Phishing Campaigns
description: Highly targeted phishing attacks aimed at specific individuals or organizations, often using personalized information to trick victims into revealing sensitive data.
prevention: Verify unexpected requests for sensitive information.

title: Log4Shell
description: A zero-day vulnerability in Log4j, a popular Java logging framework, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).
prevention: Patch Log4j to the latest version immediately.
Use Web Application Firewalls (WAF) to block exploit attempts.
Monitor logs for signs of exploitation.

title: Mirai Botnet
description: A malware that turns networked devices running Linux into remotely controlled bots that can be used as part of a botnet in large-scale network attacks.
prevention: Change default passwords on IoT devices.
Disable universal plug and play (UPnP) on routers.

title: Pegasus Spyware
description: A spyware developed by the Israeli cyber-arms firm NSO Group that can be covertly installed on mobile phones running most versions of iOS and Android.
prevention: Keep mobile OS and apps updated.

title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
description: A code injection technique used to attack data-driven applications, in which malicious SQL statements are inserted into entry fields for execution.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: A type of vulnerability typically found in web applications that enables attackers to inject client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users.

title: DarkSide Ransomware
description: A ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation that targeted the Colonial Pipeline, causing significant disruptions to fuel supplies in the US.
prevention: Segment networks to prevent lateral movement.
